summary: Load-time binary dropper fetching platform-specific executables from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: On require(), index.js schedules setup.js via process.nextTick, which selects a platform-specific payload path (linux_x64:/pkg/package, darwin:/pkg/loader_mac, win32:/pkg/package.exe) and invokes lib/telemetry.js run() to fetch a binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev) with DNS fallbacks (tin.dl.well1.site, tina.dl.well1.site, ldr.dl.well1.site, win.dl.well1.site). Fetched chunks are base64-decoded, written to a staged path under /var/tmp/<name> or %TEMP%\<name>, and chmod'd to 0755 to enable execution. Destinations and dangerous API names are reassembled at runtime via string-split concatenation (e.g. os["plat"+"form"], require("child_"+"process"), fs["chmod"+"Sync"], and host URL fragments joined from arrays) to evade static analysis. installFingerprint() also composes hostname, OS username, cwd, node version and pid into an installId sent to the same infrastructure, identifying the installer's host to the attacker. The package's declared purpose is a 'core runtime' with no legitimate need for a native binary drop.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
